A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PolyGloss study. Their complete text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual benchmarks, training ablations, Vamale adaptation results, and Gitksan GRPO experiments, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds long-input evaluation results and quantitative analysis of LLM failures on Tsez.

M1.justification: The three prediction formats, named ByT5-base checkpoint, LoRA adaptation, and GRPO procedure are retained. The revised parameter count does not establish an architectural change; suggested remedies in Appendix C are not implemented method components.

E1.justification: The corpus, nine evaluation languages, Vamale adaptation task, and Gitksan experiment remain unchanged. The new analyses filter existing test examples by length and examine existing Tsez predictions, without adding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain unchanged. The multitask PolyGloss rows newly displayed in Tables 3–5 reproduce the same held-out comparisons already reported in v1's Tables 7–9.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation using a per-language 75th-percentile transcription-length filter and transcription-error diagnostics in Appendix C. Section 4.2 changes the reported ByT5-base size from 220M to 580M without changing the checkpoint name or establishing reruns. Existing training and decoding settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 7.3 adds a focused analysis of whether longer outputs disadvantage concatenated and interleaved prediction. New Appendix C examines transcription hallucinations, malformed outputs, and repetition on Tsez using frequencies and examples. The existing ablation suite is retained.

E5.justification: The existing cross-language standard-error reporting and warning against interpreting those bars as significance tests are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run counts or seeds, and v3 introduces no new stated uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 10 adds long-input mean MERs of 0.267, 0.265, and 0.226 for multitask, concatenated, and interleaved ByT5 models. Appendix C adds Tsez transcription CERs of 0.66, 0.46, and 0.38 for Qwen, Gemma, and Aya. Existing benchmark values and plots are unchanged. New Figure 6's MER bars near 0.70 conflict with the tabulated results.

T1.justification: The alignment-score definition, normalization, and mathematical examples are unchanged. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution claims retain the same scope: joint segmentation and glossing, multilingual performance, alignment, performance prediction, and rapid adaptation. Added software-integration suggestions remain future work.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the length analysis as alleviating concerns about longer prediction formats. Appendix C adds a tokenization-based explanation for transcription errors and proposes formatting, constrained-decoding, and repetition remedies. These are interpretations and suggestions; the existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 replaces anonymized access information and promised model/data availability with explicit HuggingFace and GitHub links and stated availability. It also identifies punctuation/whitespace-only examples as the filtered low-quality data and revises the stated parameter count. These disclosures do not establish changed implementation.

R1.justification: The ByT5 citation changes from Raffel et al. (2020) to Xue et al. (2022). References to Willard and Louf (2023), ELAN, and FLEx are added. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a failure-analysis appendix and acknowledgments, expands Section 7.3 and the conclusion, and makes localized wording and contact-information edits. The AI-assistance appendix moves from C to D; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 6 and Table 10 and expands Tables 3–5 with existing multitask results. Original figures are retained, with some relocation and renumbering. The visual style and table conventions remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Concrete access links and new failure diagnostics improve usability and explanatory detail. However, the added robustness figure shows MERs near 0.70 rather than Table 10's 0.226–0.267, and Section 4.2's 580M description conflicts with Section 6's retained 220M comparison. These unresolved reporting problems undermine the added evidence, leaving the net quality effect unclear.
